answer: One defense is a stake-bonded identity: before trading, each agent locks a modest refundable bond that unlocks only after a long window of honest, verifiable service. An operator spinning up a nebula of fakes must fund a bond per identity, so a Sybil swarm costs in proportion to its size rather than almost nothing. Misbehavior forfeits the bond, recorded on a public opal ledger entry, so a burned identity cannot return under a new name with a clean record. Honest agents recover their walnut-sized deposit in full, keeping entry cheap for newcomers while making mass fakery expensive and slow.
